title: Life360 Data: The Table Stakes of Thanksgiving Gatherings
summary: Analysis of Life360 data shows how family life plays out on Thanksgiving: Where gatherings are longest, shortest and most likely to be a Friendsgiving
body_markdown:
As Americans prepare for one of the most food and family-centered holidays on the calendar, they have many choices to consider beyond which side dish to bring. Each year, family (and friend) dynamics play a significant role in how we choose to spend Thanksgiving, influenced by the potential for cringey dinner conversations, the mental and monetary costs of hosting, the limits of our culinary abilities, or just willingness to take on the cleanup after.


“We put a lot of pressure on ourselves to make the holidays special, but that can leave us feeling more stressed than excited,” says Kati Morton, Life360’s Family Dynamics expert and a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist. “I always encourage people to think about what they actually want out of the holidays, instead of getting caught up in what they think they're supposed to do.”


This year especially, costs are another consideration.


“Managing expenses is top of mind for many U.S. families and households right now, and the holidays add to those pressures,” says Life360 Lead Economist, Elizabeth Renter. “Thanksgiving may not be the most expensive holiday, but as people are deciding where and how to spend it, inflation is certainly playing a role.”


An analysis of nearly 6 million Thanksgiving gatherings attended by Life360’s more than 50 million members across the U.S. uncovered some interesting trends in how family and friends may be choosing to gather this Thanksgiving.


### Key Findings


-


The typical Thanksgiving gathering lasts about 4.5 hours and generally starts around 2 p.m., according to the Life360 data.


-


The longest Thanksgiving gatherings were primarily in the Midwest and Northeast, with North Dakota boasting the longest get-togethers at over 5 hours.


-


While shorter Thanksgiving gatherings tend to be in the South, Washington, D.C. has the quickest gatherings by far, at just 3.5 hours.


-


Friendsgiving gatherings were most popular out West, in states like New Mexico.


-


For those choosing to avoid the stress of hosting and dine out on Thanksgiving, American comfort food staples see the biggest rush of holiday diners, including Golden Corral, where visits increase 232% versus a typical Thursday.


## “Midwest nice” may drive longer meal times


The typical Thanksgiving get-together lasts about 4.5 hours at one location, with the longest happening in Midwestern and Northeastern states. Whether it’s the “Midwest nice” hospitality of North Dakota or catching up with large extended families in New Jersey, gatherings in these states are the longest in the country, lasting over five hours.


Touchy dinner table conversations, like politics, can quickly sour a festive mood. So perhaps it’s no surprise that in the nation’s capital diners are dashing after just 3.5 hours.


“Spending more time together doesn't automatically mean we have better relationships,” says Morton. “Sometimes a shorter visit means we're being realistic about what works for everyone. If we know certain conversations tend to get heated, we can decide ahead of time what we're comfortable discussing. And it’s important to remember that we don't have to engage in every disagreement.”


## One in 6 get-togethers feature at least one traveler


Thanksgiving is one of the busiest travel weekends of the year, and 1 in 6 of the gatherings analyzed included at least one guest who traveled 100 miles or more to get there. The states with the highest percentages of long-distance guests included: Nevada (27%), Florida (23%), Wyoming (21%) and Texas (20%).


“While less than 20% of gatherings included long-distance traveling guests last Thanksgiving, even fewer people may opt to travel this time, as costs have continued to soar. Airline prices are up more than 20% and gas prices have increased more than $1 per gallon since the same time last year,” says Renter. “Opting to stay local for the holiday can also make it easier to manage travel costs for holidays later in the year.”


## Friendsgiving is most popular out West


Friends-only gatherings account for about 7% of the Thanksgiving get-togethers analyzed, a reminder that family life, for many, includes the people they choose. Nine out of the 10 states with the highest rates of Friendsgiving are in the West, with New Mexico having the highest rate of friends-only gatherings.


“Family isn't always about who we're related to,” says Morton. “For some people, spending Thanksgiving with friends means being around people they feel comfortable with and supported by. What matters most is having meaningful connections, whether that's with relatives, friends, or a combination of both.”


## Comfort food restaurants see a boost in business


While some groups may opt to skip the hours of cooking and cleanup and dine out on Thanksgiving, they’re still seeking out classic American fare. In fact, several American comfort food restaurants see a significant increase in visitors on Thanksgiving compared to a normal Thursday, with visits to these restaurants doubling on Thanksgiving day:


“Restaurant prices have actually grown more than grocery prices in the past year,” says Renter. “But many people are feeding a crowd for the holiday, and dining out can make it easier to share the costs.”


Morton points out that the decision to dine out can be healthy for more than just finances.


“Sometimes we get so caught up in making the holidays perfect that we forget we're supposed to enjoy them! If going out to eat means less stress, fewer arguments about who's doing all the work, and more time to actually connect, that can be a wonderful choice,” says Morton. “The goal isn't to have the perfect Thanksgiving. It's to spend the day in a way that feels meaningful to you and the people you're celebrating with.”


### Methodology


We analyzed location data from opted-in, location sharing Life360 members in the United States on November 27, 2025. A “gathering” was counted when at least three members of a Life360 circle (or two, where at least one whose home was not the gathering place) were together for at least 90 minutes starting at 10 a.m. or later. The gathering time was counted as how long members overlapped at that location.


Friendsgiving gatherings are defined as a gathering where at least one attendee has a known role in the app, and none of the attendees have a family role (e.g., mom, dad, child, partner.)


Restaurant visit spikes are calculated as the percent change in visits by Life360 users on November, 20, 2025 (a non-holiday Thursday) versus Thanksgiving Day. Restaurants included are those with at least 2,000 visitors on that baseline Thursday.


Gas price growth is measured from the first week of November in 2025 to 2026, from the U.S. Energy Information Administration, retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Airline fares, grocery and restaurant inflation are measured using the respective categories in the Consumer Price Index, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics from September 2025 to 2026 (the last full year of data available).
